chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yahya Al-Azraq, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'If a man performs Hajj on behalf of another man, is it permissible for him to perform Tawaf on behalf of his relatives?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he has completed the rituals of Hajj, let him do whatever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person perform Tawaf on behalf of relatives while performing Hajj for someone else?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the scope of Hajj al-Ni'ab by distinguishing between the obligatory rituals specific to the proxy and the optional acts of worship. It establishes that once the core Hajj duties are fulfilled for the principal, the proxy gains the flexibility to perform additional Tawaf or other rites on behalf of different individuals, reflecting the Shia juristic view of the agent's independent capacity for subsequent worship. This highlights the practical adaptability of ritual performance in Shia fiqh, allowing for efficient delegation of religious duties among family members.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Yahya Al Arzaq who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man performs Hajj on behalf of the man, would it be correct for him if he were to circumambulate on behalf of his relatives?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he fulfils the rituals of the Hajj, so let him do whatever he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Yahya al-Azraq who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs al-Hajj for someone else; if he can perform Tawaf for his relatives. He (the Imam) said, ‘After completing the acts of al-Hajj, he can do whatever he likes/”
